All clean. Here's the summary.

## What I migrated

A deterministic codemod had already wrapped `app/llm.py`'s default `AsyncOpenAI` client construction with `router_runtime.wrap_openai()`, which transparently translates Chat Completions calls to `/v1/responses` calls against Router when `RAMP_ROUTER_API_KEY` is set (and falls back to the real provider otherwise). But that wrap only intercepts traffic when the client's `base_url` host is `api.openai.com` — and OpenManus's actual default config (`config/config.toml` / `config.example.toml`) points `base_url` straight at Anthropic's OpenAI-compat endpoint (`api.anthropic.com`), and the Jiekou.AI example does the same for a third-party host. With the host-match as-is, Router routing was a silent no-op for the app's real default configuration.

**Fix (`app/llm.py`):** pass `unlock_hosts=(host-of-configured-base_url,)` to `wrap_openai()` — a parameter the runtime already ships exactly for "another vendor's OpenAI-compatible host whose requests go to Router when their model is a Router catalog id." This makes the existing translation logic (text, streaming, images, tool calls — all already implemented in `router_runtime.chat_to_responses`/`responses_to_chat`) actually engage regardless of which OpenAI-compatible provider host the app is configured against.

**Verified** against the Router simulator: a single text-only `ask()`, a streaming `ask()`, and a tool-calling `ask_tool()` call all correctly produced `POST /v1/responses` requests to Router (model resolved from the dated snapshot `claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929` → `claude-sonnet-4-5`) with valid round-tripped responses. Router's `Authorization` header is freshly built from `RAMP_ROUTER_API_KEY` by the runtime (`_router_headers`) — the provider key configured in `config.toml` is never sent to Router, only used if a request falls back to the real provider.

**CI script (`.github/workflows/pr-autodiff.yaml`):** this workflow builds its own independent `OpenAI` client (not using `router_runtime` at all) with `secrets.OPENAI_API_KEY`/`OPENAI_BASE_URL` and calls `chat.completions.create(model="o3-mini", ...)`. Migrated it to point at Router (`RAMP_ROUTER_API_KEY`, `RAMP_ROUTER_BASE_URL` secrets) and converted the call to `client.responses.create(...)`, reading `response.output_text`. The model is now read from a `ROUTER_MODEL` repo variable rather than the hardcoded `"o3-mini"`, since valid Router model IDs are account-specific and I can't invent one — this needs to be set via the repo's GitHub Actions variables before the workflow runs again.

Local compile + full pytest suite (4 tests) still pass; nothing else touched.

## Call sites I could not migrate

- **`app/llm.py:224-228` (Azure branch, `api_type == "azure"`)** — constructs `AsyncAzureOpenAI`. `router_runtime.wrap_openai()` explicitly excludes Azure client classes by design (Azure deployment URLs aren't a simple host-swap target), so this path has no Router interception mechanism at all. Would require a structurally different approach (e.g. bypassing Azure entirely when Router is active) that goes beyond a transport-only change.
- **`app/bedrock.py:42` (`api_type == "aws"`)** — uses `boto3.client("bedrock-runtime")`, not the OpenAI/Anthropic SDK. It's not HTTP-via-httpx, so `router_runtime`'s transport-level interception can't reach it. Migrating this would mean rewriting `BedrockClient`'s custom OpenAI-shape emulation to instead call an OpenAI/Anthropic SDK client against Router — a business-logic rewrite, not a transport swap.

Both are pre-existing, optional config profiles (not the shipped default) and are unaffected by my changes — they keep working exactly as before, just outside Router's reach.
